name: dmalloc
desc: Debug versions of system memory management routines
why: Debug malloc library that instruments heap allocations; a close call, interesting for memory archaeology but niche.

brief.what_it_is: Dmalloc is a debug memory allocation library for C programs. It is a drop-in replacement for the system's malloc, realloc, calloc, free and related memory routines, so a program is relinked or preloaded against it rather than changed in its calls. It takes ordinary heap activity from the program and reports problems such as leaks, overruns and bad frees, along with statistics. The package includes the library, configuration scripts, a debug utility application, a test program and documentation. Its own description calls it the 'debug memory allocation' or dmalloc library.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents it as a way to get powerful memory debugging, configurable at runtime, without rewriting the program around a special allocator. The features it lists are memory-leak tracking, fence-post write detection, file/line number reporting, and logging of statistics.
brief.how_it_works: The README I read does not explain the internals. It says the library replaces the standard allocation calls and that its debugging facilities are configured at runtime, which is controlled through the DMALLOC_OPTIONS environment variable. It also says it supports debugging threaded programs.
brief.install_notes: The homepage mentions configuration scripts, which suggests a configure-and-make build, but I did not see the build steps. The GitHub repository and getting-started docs I tried to fetch both returned 404, so I could not confirm the install or first-run steps. Runtime behaviour is set through the DMALLOC_OPTIONS environment variable.
brief.standout: Runtime-configurable checks on an ordinary malloc replacement, with a long portability list that includes old and obscure systems such as Unicos on a Cray T3E, DG/UX and Ultrix. The author has kept it going as a personal project for decades, which makes it a piece of memory-debugging history.
brief.status: Unknown. The homepage has a ChangeLog link and says support is through GitHub issues, but it shows no release date or version. I could not reach the GitHub repository (github.com/dmalloc/dmalloc returned 404) or the docs page I guessed, so I have no commit or release date.
brief.caveats: The portability list on the homepage includes 'MS-DOG' and 'Windoze', which are presumably jokes or stale entries, and I did not check any of them. The sidebar lists unrelated personal pages (a spam filter, an Android ORM, an eggnog recipe), which suggests the site belongs to one author and not to a project team. I could not confirm the exact GitHub URL, so the repository link is unverified. The library is ISC-licensed according to the homepage, while the webpages are CC BY-SA 3.0.
quotes: The debug memory allocation or dmalloc library has been designed as a drop in replacement for the system's malloc, realloc, calloc, free and other memory management routines while providing powerful debugging facilities configurable at runtime.
These facilities include such things as memory-leak tracking, fence-post write detection, file/line number reporting, and general logging of statistics.
Please include the version number of the library that you are using, your machine and operating system types, and the value of the DMALLOC_OPTIONS environment variable.
